ud3.10:1.1: I have heard that on one occasion,
ud3.10:1.2: the Blessed One was staying at Uruvelā on the bank of the Nerañjarā River at the root of the Bodhi tree–the tree of awakening–newly awakened.
ud3.10:1.3: And on that occasion he sat at the root of the Bodhi tree for seven days in one session, sensitive to the bliss of release.
ud3.10:2.1: Then, with the passing of seven days, after emerging from that concentration, he surveyed the world with the eye of an Awakened One.
ud3.10:2.2: As he did so, he saw living beings burning with the many fevers and aflame with the many fires born of passion,
ud3.10:3.1: Then, on realizing the significance of that, he on that occasion exclaimed:
ud3.10:4.2: Afflicted by contact, it calls disease a ‘self.’
ud3.10:5.1: it becomes otherwise than that. Becoming otherwise, the world is attached to becoming,
ud3.10:5.2: afflicted by becoming, and yet delights in that very becoming.
ud3.10:5.3: Where there’s delight, there is fear.
ud3.10:6.1: Whatever contemplatives or brahmans say that liberation from becoming is by means of becoming, all of them are not released from becoming, I say.
ud3.10:6.2: And whatever contemplatives or brahmans say that escape from becoming is by means of non-becoming, all of them have not escaped from becoming, I say.
ud3.10:7.1: For this stress comes into play in dependence on every acquisition. With the ending of every clinging/sustenance, there’s no stress coming into play.
ud3.10:7.3: Beings, afflicted with thick ignorance, are unreleased from passion for what has come to be.
ud3.10:7.4: All levels of becoming, anywhere, in any way, are inconstant, stressful, subject to change.
ud3.10:8.2: Seeing this–as it’s come to be– with right discernment,
ud3.10:8.5: From the total ending of craving
ud3.10:8.6: comes fading & cessation without remainder: unbinding.
ud3.10:9.2: For the monk unbound through lack of clinging/sustenance, there’s no further becoming.
ud3.10:9.3: He has conquered Māra, won the battle,
